title: Existence of prefix deletion equivalence
statement: Let I be a linearly ordered type, p≥0, n=p+2 and t:Fin(n)→I. Use cechStableSort and cechPartialSort [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]. Let O consist of (σ,a,τ,r) with σ,τ permutations of Fin(n), a:Fin(n), r:Fin(n+1), σ stable for t, τ partial sorted with prefix a, and r<a. Let N consist of (j,ρ,b,η) with j:Fin(n), ρ,η permutations of Fin(n-1), b:Fin(n-1), ρ stable for t∘j.succAbove, η partial sorted with prefix b, and (t(j),j) strictly preceding (t(j.succAbove(ρ(b))),j.succAbove(ρ(b))) lexicographically. There exists e:O≃N such that for e(σ,a,τ,r)=(j,ρ,b,η), a=b+1, r<n and τ(r)=j. This statement does not assert the two permutation restriction identities.

proof.text: For outgoing (σ,a,τ,r), r<a<n gives j=σ(r)=τ(r). Restrict both permutations to the complements of r and j via the increasing successor bijections, and put b=a-1. Stable order, prefix agreement and increasing tails persist; the junction follows the omitted pair because r<a.

For incoming (j,ρ,b,η), insert j into both permutations at its stable rank r. The before condition gives r≤b; set a=b+1. The resulting σ is stable and τ partial sorted. Deletion and insertion are inverse since the stable rank is unique. Thus this is an equivalence with a=b+1 and τ(r)=j. See the Lean docstring for the position and label inequalities and boundary cases.

theorem prefixDeletionExistence {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I) :
    ∃ e : ({x : Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)) × Fin (p + 2) ×
      Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 2)) × Fin (p + 3) //
    (cechStableSort t x.1 ∧ cechPartialSort x.1 x.2.2.1 x.2.1) ∧
      x.2.2.2.val < x.2.1.val}) ≃
      ({y : Fin (p + 2) × Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) × Fin (p + 1) ×
      Equiv.Perm (Fin (p + 1)) //
    (cechStableSort (t ∘ y.1.succAbove) y.2.1 ∧
      cechPartialSort y.2.1 y.2.2.2 y.2.2.1) ∧
    (t y.1 < t (y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)) ∨
      (t y.1 = t (y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)) ∧
        y.1 < y.1.succAbove (y.2.1 y.2.2.1)))}), ∀ x,
      let y := e x
      x.1.2.1.val = y.1.2.2.1.val + 1 ∧
      ∃ hr : x.1.2.2.2.val < p + 2,
        x.1.2.2.1 ⟨x.1.2.2.2.val, hr⟩ = y.1.1
